newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steelmakers cut 6-month profit forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Japan steelmakers cut 6-month profit forecasts.

text.p: Japanese steelmakers on Wednesday lowered their profit forecasts for the six months to September 30, 1996 largely due to a delay in inventory adjustments.
Among the top five makers, all except NKK Corp lowered their half-year profit forecasts.
Industry leader Nippon Steel Corp, for example, lowered its outlook for the six-month parent current profit to 25 billion yen ($229 million) from its May forecast of 35 billion yen ($321 million).

Its actual half-year parent current profit in 1995/96 was 29.38 billion yen ($269 million). Current profit is a pre-tax profit which includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

"Demand and supply in the steel industry is showing signs of recovery. But Japan's crude steel output in the first half of this business year is expected to remain as low as that of the second half of last business year due to a drastic cut in output for inventory adjustment," Nippon Steel said in a statement.

Steel stocks have piled up due to oversupply, industry analysts said. Steelmakers said they had expected larger demand for steel construction materials due to reconstruction following the massive earthquake in Kobe in January last year and the recovery in Japan's overall economy.
Steelmakers have said since late last year that they are cutting output to reduce inventories, but industry analysts say the level of inventories remains high.
The oversupply has cut prices of steel products, steelmakers say.
Sumitomo Metal Industries Ltd said a fall in steel exports and higher costs for materials were other reasons for the lowered profit forecasts.
NKK said it maintained its previous forecast for half-year current profit of 10 billion yen ($91.7 million), helped by its efforts at cost-cutting both in its steel and engineering divisions.

Sumitomo Metal and Kobe Steel Ltd lowered their forecast for full-year parent current profit while Nippon Steel maintained its forecast for the full year. NKK dropped its forecast for the year but the reason was not immediately clear.

"In the second half of fiscal 1996, Kobe Steel does not foresee a sharp recovery of the economy. Although the company hopes the business environment will improve, it views the situation as difficult," Kobe Steel said in a statement.
Nippon Steel said: "We will make utmost efforts to achieve 90 billion yen in parent current profit for the full year." ($1=109 yen)
